# Klarity Disk

> Klarity Disk is a disk space analyzer for the Mac, sold on the Mac App Store as a one-time purchase (usually $6.99 in the US; the store shows the price in each country). It scans a folder, the whole disk or an external drive and draws it as a treemap or icicle chart, with each folder coloured by how long since it last changed, and it has a Large Files list that ranks every file in the scan by size, largest first. It needs macOS 14.6 or later, has no network access, no account and no analytics, and is made by one independent developer, Mukul Mehra.

Key facts:

- It is not a cleaner. It deletes nothing by itself: items go to the Trash only after the user confirms, and folders of 1 GB or more need a slide to confirm. The home folder, Library, Keychains and system folders are refused; other risky places get an extra warning first.
- Macworld reviewed version 1.1 in April 2026 (4 out of 5) and found permission errors when deleting apps. Since version 1.3 (September 2026) Klarity asks for access once per disk, and moving the user's own files to the Trash works. Items macOS protects, such as apps from the App Store, still have to be deleted in Finder with an administrator password; Klarity says so instead of showing an error.
- It cannot scan as an administrator, cannot see inside Time Machine local snapshots, and has no free trial.
- It also shows memory use in the menu bar.
